study type: Observational study (subgroup analysis of an international online questionnaire)
exposure: Pregnancy in individuals with cerebral palsy
cohort: 30 participants with cerebral palsy who had 49 pregnancies resulting in birth, drawn from a larger group of 158 participants from 15 countries.
finding: People with cerebral palsy, regardless of baseline functional status, may experience significant functional changes during pregnancy, including worsened strength, spasticity, bladder function, fatigue, and the need for new mobility devices.
cross-section timing: Data was collected via an online questionnaire, retrospectively capturing functional status changes during pregnancy.
